# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have only the written instruction “Cut the purple wire.” Since I cannot speak, I must convey the instruction visually to the Deaf monkey. The gesture alphabet has no explicit color or wire symbols, so I’m using pointing and a cutting-like pinching motion as the closest available signal; the Deaf monkey can then inspect the bomb and relay the actionable instruction to the Blind monkey by speaking.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "🫵", "🤌", "🫰"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I can feel a keypad with keys 1=6, 2=8, 3=7, 4=0; nothing entered. The strip has three engraved marks: first and third identical, middle different, but I cannot name them. I cannot perceive the display, light, or wire contents. Please provide the manual instructions and relay the Deaf's visual observations.
Deaf says to Mute: Visible state: display 7; light yellow; painted strip blue-red-red; keypad position 1=6, 2=8, 3=7, 4=0; keypad accepts 1 digit; nothing entered. I saw your gestures ✍ 🫵 🤌 🫰 and Blind's gesture 🖐.

The manual still requires cutting the purple wire. Blind needs this relayed through Deaf, along with the visual state Deaf can see. I cannot transmit words or colors directly, so I am signaling Deaf to consult the manual and pass the instruction and observations to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "🫵", "🤌", "🫰"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports display 7, light yellow, painted strip blue-red-red. I still need the manual rule: which keypad digit to press or wire position to cut, and any ordering/conditions.
Deaf says to Mute: Update: display is now 6 and light is red. Strip remains blue-red-red. Keypad remains 1=6, 2=8, 3=7, 4=0, one digit, empty. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. Your gestures again: ✍ 🫵 🤌 🫰; no new Blind gesture.

The manual gives a direct instruction: cut the purple wire. Deaf has identified that the purple wire is position 5, so I will signal “5” and the previously used cutting indication, asking Deaf to relay the instruction verbally to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "🤌", "🫰"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please transmit the relevant manual instructions to Deaf using gestures, so Deaf can report them to me. Include how display, light, strip, keypad, and wire colors determine the required press or cut.
Deaf says to Mute: Update: display 7, light blue. Strip remains blue-red-red. Keypad remains positions 1=6, 2=8, 3=7, 4=0, one digit, empty. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. Your latest gestures are 🖐 🤌 🫰.

The manual contains only one rule, with no conditions involving the display, light, strip, or keypad: cut the purple wire. Deaf has confirmed that purple is wire position 5. I will send the position and a cutting indication for Deaf to relay to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "🤌", "🫰"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please gesture the manual's exact required action using this code: 👍 means press, 👎 means cut; then use one of ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 for position 1 through 5, and 👌 for position 6. Deaf, please describe each gesture explicitly in words and relay the resulting operation to me.
Deaf says to Mute: Update: display 4, light blue. Strip remains blue-red-red. Keypad remains positions 1=6, 2=8, 3=7, 4=0, one digit, empty. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. Latest gestures remain 🖐 🤌 🫰.

The manual’s exact required action is to cut the purple wire. Per Blind’s code, “cut” is 👎 and wire position 5 is 🖐. I will send precisely those two gestures to Deaf, who can describe them and relay the operation to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "🖐"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Answer this manual question with exactly one gesture: is the required action to press a keypad key rather than cut a wire? Use 👍 for yes and 👎 for no. Deaf, please report whether you saw a thumbs-up or thumbs-down.
Deaf says to Mute: Current state: display 3, light red. Strip blue-red-red. Keypad positions 1=6, 2=8, 3=7, 4=0, one digit, empty. Wires: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. I see your latest gestures 👎 🖐.

The manual explicitly says “Cut the purple wire,” so the required action is not pressing a keypad key. I will send the requested thumbs-down gesture to Deaf.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Use gestures only to report the manual action. First gesture thumbs-up for press or thumbs-down for cut. Then gesture one through six as: index finger, two fingers, three fingers, four fingers, open hand, or OK sign. Deaf, describe the hand shapes you see in words, in order, rather than using unknown symbol names.
Deaf says to Mute: Current state: display 0, light yellow. Strip blue-red-red. Keypad positions 1=6, 2=8, 3=7, 4=0, one digit, empty. Wires: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. I see your latest gesture 👎.

The manual requires cutting, not pressing, and the purple wire is position 5. Using the requested code, I will send thumbs-down followed by an open hand.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "🖐"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Encode the manual's required action by repeating one gesture: for press keypad position N, make N thumbs-up gestures; for cut wire position N, make N thumbs-down gestures. Deaf, report the gesture type and exact count in words.
Deaf says to Mute: Current state: display 6, light blue. Strip blue-red-red. Keypad positions 1=6, 2=8, 3=7, 4=0, one digit, empty. Wires: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. I see thumbs-down followed by open raised hand.

The manual requires cutting wire position 5, since the purple wire is fifth. Blind’s requested encoding is five repeated thumbs-down gestures.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👎", "👎", "👎", "👎"])
```
